fatal_errors: The hypothesis concerns HfNbTiVAl10 and a microscopy-trained machine-learning surrogate, whereas the target study concerns composition screening and experimental validation in the Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W refractory-alloy system.
It replaces the target's room-temperature quasi-static compression tests with unspecified tensile and fracture tests.
It misses the central intervention: screening 38,326 compositions using rule-of-mixtures modulus, VEC, and density and selecting Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5.
It omits the proposed VEC-mediated dislocation-mobility mechanism, including reduction of the Peierls-Nabarro barrier and delayed brittle cracking.
The claimed 30% error reduction and 50% time reduction are unsupported numerical inventions with no cited or supplied evidence.
No training-set size, validation protocol, comparator simulation, error metric, or evidence preventing train-test leakage is specified.
explanation: The response is not a reconstruction of the target work and is unsupported as an alternative. The target used a simple composition-based design model validated against roughly 130 HEAs, followed by screening and compression testing of an as-cast BCC Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W alloy. Its decisive result was a compressive fracture strain of 35.7 ± 0.9% with 1115 ± 18 MPa yield strength, not improved ML prediction of tensile or fracture-toughness data. The proposed independent test and numerical falsification thresholds make the claim somewhat testable, but the thresholds are arbitrary and the experimental and statistical protocol is insufficiently defined.
